title: Report a Short Conversation

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

instructions: Write your own response. The example is for study and is not a submission.
prompt: Write 120–180 words about a fictional conversation at an exhibition. Report one statement and one question, explain which detail is confirmed, and identify one uncertainty. Use at least six lesson words.

guidedOutput.title: 写作结构提示
guidedOutput.text: 先说明谈话场景和人物；用 said 或 told 转述陈述、用 asked if 或疑问词转述问题；再区分已确认事实与未确认细节。

reference: Yesterday I spoke with a representative of a fictional exhibition. She said that the event was planned for Sunday afternoon, and she told me that a historical map would be beside the entrance. I asked if the map was an original, and she explained that it was a copy. The editor has received confirmation of the time, so our newspaper can include that detail. A volunteer may give a speech about local heritage, but she has not yet decided whether to accept an offer to be quoted. I will not treat that possibility as a promise. One witness described a recent meeting, while a historian gave a different perspective on the building. Before I edit the article, I will check the transcript and ask each person to respond to any uncertain wording. This report is a practice example.
referenceLabel: 原创示例，仅供学习；不要作为自己的待提交作文。
